title: He Fell 22,000 Feet With No Parachute… and Lived
format: viral-short (~70 s, one reveal, loop ending, on-screen FOLLOW)
style: flat cartoon silhouettes (Dillinger parts), cuts on the music beat but softer: no cut flash, small punch, new framing every 8 beats
lines: Twenty two thousand feet. No parachute. And this man lived.
January 3rd, 1943. Alan Magee was a ball turret gunner on a B-17 bomber, over Saint-Nazaire, in occupied France.
German flak tore into the plane, and it started to spin.
Magee climbed out of his turret, and found his parachute ripped to shreds.
So he jumped anyway. At that height there's barely any air. He blacked out.
He fell more than four miles.
He smashed through the glass roof of the Saint-Nazaire railway station. The glass slowed him down, just enough.
Twenty eight wounds. A broken leg. His arm nearly torn off. But he was alive.
German soldiers found him on the station floor, and their doctors saved his life.
He spent the rest of the war as a prisoner, and went home in 1945.
Fifty years later, the people of Saint-Nazaire built a memorial to him and his crew.
He lived to be eighty four.

notes: Sources: Wikipedia 'Alan Magee'; 303rd Bomb Group Association (303rdbg.com/magee.html); WeAreTheMighty. Alan Eugene Magee (1919-2003), ball turret gunner, 360th BS / 303rd BG, B-17F 'Snap! Crackle! Pop!'. 3 Jan 1943 raid on Saint-Nazaire; flak damage, aircraft spinning; his parachute was damaged/unusable; he jumped and lost consciousness (altitude/oxygen); fell ~22,000 ft (some sources 20,000; 'over four miles'); crashed through the glass roof of the Saint-Nazaire railway station; 28 shrapnel wounds, broken right leg and ankle, right arm nearly severed; treated by German doctors; POW until May 1945. 3 Jan 1993: Saint-Nazaire unveiled a memorial to Magee and his crew. Died 20 Dec 2003 in San Angelo, Texas, aged 84. Wording written from scratch (not copied from the social post the owner shared).
